rationale: The child accounts are closed, so this update makes the main question's account match the evidence actually held and states the conditions the effect depends on. The Node-interface receipt is folded in (the same state change is now observed on a real Node started by RestartNode, not only on synchronous RawNodes), which removes the last scope objection that this was a test-harness artefact, and two boundary conditions are made explicit from source rather than left implicit: the forged message only helps a candidate because the lease test it defeats requires CheckQuorum, and it affects followers only - a leader treats the same type as a no-op, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term. Nothing in the severity account changes; the earlier bounds (per-message effect, repair by the next leader message, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the type, no committed-entry loss after the forged election) stand.

interpretations.rationale: Current account across five receipts. A MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted with no error through both documented inbound paths - RawNode.Step (index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7, reproduced at 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a) and the real Node interface that applications use, where the node's own reported leader went 1 -> 0 and the same transition was produced by the intended local API Node.ForgetLeader (indices 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40, with the local-type control holding at 41). It changes the support a follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15 and 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window per message is closed by the next genuine leader message (heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick, index 7, and the same pre-vote was ignored again, index 8), but a sender repeating the message each round keeps it open without any repair failing: three consecutive rounds restored the context and granted again (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm stays bounded: after the forged election the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so no committed entry was lost. Cause and controls are unchanged: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and because the wire form carries no term field Step treats it as a local message and skips term checks; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected or ignored in every receipt. Conditions the effect depends on, stated explicitly: the defeated lease test exists only when Config.CheckQuorum is set (inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout), so the marginal effect of the forged message is specific to CheckQuorum deployments; the type is a no-op on leaders, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term; and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate, so the message does not manufacture support for stale candidates. Remaining limits are scope: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the message outright, and the persistence loop using an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that followers grant pre-votes and votes regardless of their leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the control round inside the persistence loop and the Node-interface control.
The change is per-message and reversible: the context returns with the next real leader heartbeat in every round, so this is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver a protobuf message of any type - including one the module only produces locally - to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss, authentication or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
The quorum-scale election was measured on one voter plus the candidate in the earlier receipt and not re-measured under the repeated cadence.
The incumbent is observed only through the first append from the new leader, so the length of any overlap between two leaders under delayed message delivery is not quantified.
The effect requires CheckQuorum to be enabled for the lease test it defeats, and it is a follower-side change only (leaders ignore the type).
interpretations.joint_history: All five cited receipts are separate executions of one fixed-experiment lineage in the same package with the same construction: three real RawNode instances (plus, in the last one, a real Node started by RestartNode) built from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1 with voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, a real election for node 1 and messages delivered through the public Step path. CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 is the original harness; CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 is its revised successor (previous_id = the original) adding the repair-path and quorum scenarios; CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a adds the aftermath scenario with per-stream event names; CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849 adds the per-round persistence loop; CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40 adds the real Node interface scenario. Each run builds its own instances and prints into its own runner stream, so no cited index depends on another run's bytes; where the same predicate is witnessed in several receipts it is because the harness re-executed the scenario, never because observations were joined across runs.
